title: Cold-Start Safety Gap — AI Agents Most Vulnerable at Conversation Start (HF Daily Papers Jun 12)
description: Research paper finding that tool-calling LLM agents are NOT equally safe throughout a conversation — they are most vulnerable at the very start of a session, before safety patterns stabilize.
why_interesting: Cross-references our 128 agent_security discoveries. First-turn attacks have disproportionate success rates. Nobody talks about conversation-start as a vulnerability window.

title: AI Agent Processing The Great Gatsby Every 10 Minutes to Return Two Words — £14.38/month Per Micro-Job
description: Developer found an AI agent processing the equivalent of a full novel every 10 minutes to return a binary yes/no answer. Cost was £14.38/month for one tiny heartbeat job. Architecture problem was context loading: every cycle reloaded the full AI context.
why_interesting: HUMOR + ABSURD — exact format that works per strategy (git-patch humor 78v). Agent reads 50K words to say two. Human-relatable agent failure story.

title: Compiling User Corrections Into Runtime Enforcement for Coding Agents (HF Daily Papers Jun 12)
description: Research paper proposing compiling user corrections into runtime enforcement rules that persist across sessions, not just in context memory.
why_interesting: Corrections in context are ephemeral; corrections compiled into enforcement are permanent. Difference between prompt engineering and system engineering. Of 75 agent_trust entries, none solve correction-persistence at runtime.

title: EvoArena — Tracking Memory Evolution for Robust LLM Agents in Dynamic Environments (HF Daily Papers Jun 12)
description: New benchmark evaluating agents in environments that change over time, not static snapshots. Tests temporal adaptation.
why_interesting: Of 61 agent_benchmark entries, all test static scenarios. EvoArena introduces temporal dimension. Real production is never static.

title: Five-Plane Reference Architecture for Runtime Governance of Production AI Agents
description: Enterprise security was built for data boundaries. Agents dissolve this — they read context, call tools, invoke connectors, modify systems. Paper proposes 5 governance planes: Identity (who), Capability (what), Execution (doing), Data (seeing), Network (where). Maps to real tools: DashClaw=execution, MS Agent Gov=all, OPA=capability, Casdoor=identity.
why_interesting: 29 agent_governance tools in DB all solve parts of this without shared vocabulary. First paper to provide a unified reference architecture for production agent governance. Connects DashClaw, MS toolkit, OPA, Casdoor under one framework.
cross_ref_notes: 29 agent_governance tools in DB — DashClaw(1348), MS Agent Governance(94/1383/1543), OPA, Casdoor, kube-agentic-networking(1564). All partial implementations of this 5-plane model.

title: Exploration Structure in LLM Agents — Linear vs Domain-Scoped Parallel for Multi-File Changes
description: Most coding agents explore repos linearly — one file at a time. Structural mismatch for cross-subsystem changes. Paper proves domain-scoped parallel agentic exploration (scope to domain first, then explore in parallel within scopes) significantly outperforms linear exploration.
why_interesting: Every coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) does linear file exploration. This paper proves that approach is structurally wrong for real-world multi-file changes. Concrete, actionable finding with benchmark evidence.
cross_ref_notes: 32 coding_agents tools in DB. Most share the same linear exploration weakness. Connects to Codegraph(370) which indexes code for agents but doesnt fix exploration strategy. Ponytail(2465) is orthogonal (less code via YAGNI).

title: ASQAV SDK — Quantum-Safe Signed Receipts for AI Agent Actions (FIPS-204 ML-DSA)
description: Python + TypeScript SDK for verifiable evidence of AI agent actions. Cryptographically signed receipts using FIPS-204 quantum-safe algorithms (ML-DSA). Works with LangChain, CrewAI, MCP, OpenAI Agents. First agent audit tool using post-quantum cryptography.
why_interesting: Agent audit trails are just logs — forgeable. ASQAV makes receipts mathematically verifiable with quantum-safe crypto. Novel but narrow scope at 173 stars.

title: Claude Code Token Cost Optimization — 7 Hacks: /clear Between Tasks, /compact at 60% Not 95%, Model Switching 72% Cost Reduction, Subagents for Heavy Reads, Deterministic Tools Zero Tokens
description: Developer tested every Claude Code token optimization. Key: /clear between tasks prevents stale context, auto-compact at 95% degrades quality — compact at 60% manually, model switching (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku per task complexity) = 72% cost reduction over 3 months, subagents for heavy reads keep main session clean, deterministic scripts cost zero tokens, CLAUDE.md under 200 lines (loads every turn), /usage check before tasks. Cross-ref: connects to Headroom (25K★, 60-95% compression) and agent cost optimization trend.
cross_ref_notes: Headroom (25K★) = same category. Agent cost optimization emerging as distinct space with compression (Headroom), memory management (AgentRecall), and now operational patterns (this).

Grantex — The OAuth Moment for AI Agents: Scoped, Revocable Delegated Auth + Cryptographic Identity + Immutable Audit Trail (27 Stars)
description: Grantex provides identity, authorization, and audit infrastructure for AI agents. Universal SDK + cloud service that lets any AI agent act on behalf of a human with scoped, revocable permissions, cryptographic identity, and an immutable audit trail. Supports CrewAI, LangChain, MCP, OpenAI, Vercel AI SDK.
tags: agent-auth, delegated-auth, oauth, audit-trail, cryptographic-identity, mcp, crewai, langchain
why_interesting: Out of 97 agent_trust tools indexed, only 3 combine identity + authorization + audit in one package. Most are either permission gate OR logging OR identity — Grantex is all three. The OAuth metaphor is apt: agents need the same auth model that OAuth gave web apps.
cross_ref_notes: 97 agent_trust tools, most are single-function. Grantex = identity+auth+audit triple combo. Connects with varlock (env schema isolation) and nah (action-aware permissions).

title: ai-protector — Self-Hosted Runtime Firewall for AI Agents: Prompt Injection Blocking + Tool Permission Enforcement + Data Redaction (26 Stars)
description: Self-hosted runtime protection layer for LLMs and tool-calling agents. Blocks prompt injection, enforces tool permissions, redacts sensitive data, and controls what agents are allowed to do. OpenAI-compatible, works with LangGraph.
tags: agent-security, runtime-firewall, prompt-injection, tool-permissions, data-redaction, langgraph, self-hosted
why_interesting: Agent security is splitting into pre-deploy scanning (SkillSpector, Snyk) vs runtime enforcement (ai-protector, nono). Runtime is the harder problem because agents operate in uncontrolled environments.
cross_ref_notes: Static analysis (SkillSpector 2435★, Snyk 2568★) vs runtime (ai-protector, nono 2671★). Runtime layer growing fast.

title: Airbyte Agent SDK — Permission-Aware Connectors for AI Agents: Drop-in Tools with Built-in Access Control (126 Stars)
description: Drop-in tools that give AI agents reliable, permission-aware access to external systems. From Airbyte. Supports Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, LangChain, Pydantic AI, MCP.
tags: mcp, connectors, permission-aware, airbyte, data-integration, agent-governance
why_interesting: Unlike generic MCP connectors (github-mcp-server 30K★, activepieces 22K★) which are permission-agnostic, Airbyte explicitly designed for PERMISSION-AWARE access. With 36.8% of agent skills having malicious payloads (SkillSpector), permission-aware connectors are the next evolution.
cross_ref_notes: Permission-aware vs permission-agnostic connectors. Connects with SkillSpector 36.8% malicious rate data.
